what: Seven US counties switched to punched-card voting with computer tallying for the 1964 presidential election.

sources.title: Electronic voting
sources.quote: Their first widespread use was in the US where 7 counties switched to this method for the 1964 presidential election.

note: Looked for earlier uses: Norden Electronic Vote Tallying System (mark-sense, reported by search results as first used in Kern County, CA in 1962) but the date could not be fetched from an allowed host, and Wikipedia only says 'in the 1960s'; IBM 1936 dial machine for STV ballots is a punched-card tabulation design with no sourced election use; lever machines are mechanical. 1964 kept, but a 1962 Norden use probably predates it.

what: By the 1996 US presidential election punched-card systems with computer tabulation were used by over a third of registered US voters.

sources.title: Voting machine
sources.quote: By the 1996 Presidential election, some variation of the punched card system was used by 37.3% of registered voters in the United States.

note: Searched for an earlier date at which punched-card voting passed a third of voters: search results (not fetchable here) give about 29-30% in 1980 and about 37% by 1988, so 1996 is probably too late by several years, but no fetchable source gives an earlier figure. Kept the sourced 1996 value.

what: Harvard researchers (the Schwitzgebel brothers) developed portable transceivers that recorded the location of volunteers.

sources.title: Electronic tagging
sources.quote: Portable transceivers that could record the location of volunteers were first developed by a group of researchers at Harvard University in the early 1960s.

note: Looked for earlier person or vehicle tracking: early radio direction finding and LORAN-C vehicle location (1970s) are later or undated; Schwitzgebel Harvard work is the earliest dated person tracker found. Source gives only 'early 1960s'; year 1962 is an estimate.

what: Judge Jack Love persuaded Michael Goss to found NIMCOS, which built radio ankle transmitters used to monitor offenders from a telephone-linked receiver.

sources.title: Electronic tagging
sources.quote: in 1982, an Arizona state district judge, Jack Love, convinced a former sales representative of Honeywell Information Systems, Michael T. Goss

note: Looked for earlier practical tracking of people: Schwitzgebel was a research prototype with volunteers; AVL for vehicles is 1970s or undated. NIMCOS 1982 stands; the first probationer use (1983) is later.

what: IBM developed a way of attaching magnetic stripes to plastic cards under a US government contract for a security system.

sources.title: Magnetic stripe card
sources.quote: In 1960, IBM built upon the magnetic tape idea and developed a reliable way of securing magnetic stripes to plastic cards

note: IBM magnetic-stripe card 1960 under a US government security contract; conflicts with the 1969 Parry account in the same article. Earlier machine-read cards found (Charga-Plate 1928 was imprinted, not machine-read; Hollerith cards are not identity tokens; smart-card patents 1967+ and Honeywell punched-card access 1965 are later). Kept.

what: The Rochester Institute of Technology 'VALI-DINE' system used cards with mechanically punched holes, read by machine, to let students into dining halls.

sources.title: Campus card
sources.quote: Electronic card access has been available on campuses since as early as 1968.

sources.title: Campus card
sources.quote: relied on cards with mechanically punched holes to allow access to their dining halls.

note: Replaces 1975 VingCard (1975 launch, first hotel install 1978). Campus card article dates RIT VALI-DINE card access to 1968, a machine-read identity/access card in real use. Search results also mention a 1965 Honeywell punched-card access system but it is unsourced. Hand-geometry Identimat (1970s) is later.

what: J. H. Wegstein at the US National Bureau of Standards developed computer models of fingerprints to automate their analysis, leading to AFIS.

sources.title: Identix Incorporated
sources.quote: In the 1960s, J. H. Wegstein at the National Bureau of Standards developed computer models for fingerprint representations

note: Wegstein's NBS computer fingerprint work dated only 'the 1960s'; Wikipedia lists his 1968 NBS reports and search results say the FBI approached NBS in 1963. 1965 is an estimate within the sourced decade. No earlier machine fingerprint matcher found; Identimat is hand geometry.

what: Apple introduced Touch ID fingerprint unlocking on the iPhone 5s, putting fingerprint readers in millions of ordinary phones.

sources.title: Touch ID
sources.quote: the iPhone 5s was unveiled on September 10, 2013, and was the first phone on a major US carrier to feature the technology.

note: Looked for earlier fingerprint phones or mass use: earlier fingerprint phones (e.g. Pantech 2004, Atrix 2011) were niche, and Touch ID made it routine. Kept.

what: EyeDentify's retinal scanner went on the market as a commercial model in 1981 (specific scanner means patented 1978), after the device concept emerged in 1975.

sources.title: Retinal scan
sources.quote: In 1978, specific means for a retinal scanner was patented, followed by a commercial model in 1981.

note: The concept covers retina as well as iris; retina scanning predates Daugman's 1994 iris algorithms. 1981 is the first dated working (commercial) retinal scanner found; Flom and Safir's iris concept and the 1935 Simon-Goldstein retina idea had no working device. A demonstration may precede 1981 (patent 1978) but no dated demonstration found.

what: The Bochum face-recognition system, by 1997 outperforming other systems, was sold commercially as ZN-Face to operators of airports and other busy locations.

sources.title: Facial recognition system
sources.quote: was sold commercially on the market as ZN-Face to operators of airports and other busy locations.

note: Earlier than Mexico 2000. The same article says West Virginia and New Mexico DMVs were first to use automated face recognition after 1993 (search results say West Virginia from 1998), but no dated source was fetchable. 1997 comes from ZN-Face commercial sale to airports, so it is a rough date.

what: Apple announced Face ID on the iPhone X, bringing face recognition to ordinary phone unlocking.

sources.title: Face ID
sources.quote: Apple announced Face ID alongside the iPhone X on September 12, 2017

note: Introduction date, not a measured adoption figure. Earlier face-unlock phones (e.g. Android 4.0 Face Unlock, 2011) were niche and unreliable. Kept.

what: Herman Hollerith's electromechanical punched-card tabulator was used to process the 1890 US census.

sources.title: Unit record equipment
sources.quote: Hollerith's method was used in the 1890 census.

sources.title: Unit record equipment
sources.quote: The tabulator used electromechanical relays to increment mechanical counters.

note: The definition says 'computers and machines' doing clerical work, so machines count. Hollerith's tabulator is the earliest machine for mass clerical record processing; payroll and accounting uses of unit-record equipment followed. This is a judgement call: the census is government record processing, not an office as such. LEO I (1951) was the first business computer application but is later.
